Hi all! I've formalized four of the five Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms for singular homology in Lean 4 / Mathlib (coefficients in an arbitrary ring R): homotopy invariance, the dimension axiom, long exact sequence of a pair, and additivity. Excision is still to come. [link]

The proofs work but are very rough. One notable limitation: homotopy invariance is currently only proved for ModuleCat R (the proof goes through the Eilenberg–Zilber cross product, which I've only constructed for module categories). The other three axioms are proved for a general abelian category with appropriate hypotheses. Generalizing homotopy invariance to the abelian category setting is something I'd like to do, but I'm not sure yet what the right level of generality is — any thoughts on this would also be welcome.

I'd love guidance before submitting a PR. Here are the main pain points I'd like to clean up - if anyone knows better patterns for these I'd really appreciate the pointers:

1. eqToHom proliferation from Nat.add non-definitional-equality. The Leibniz rule proof (universalSimplexCrossProduct_boundary) alone is ~300 lines, much of it shuttling eqToHom morphisms through SimplexCategory.toTop using eqToHom_map + ← Functor.map_comp. The root cause is that associativity/commutativity of + in degrees isn't definitional. I worked around some of this (e.g. ordering X ⨯ Δ[1] rather than Δ[1] ⨯ X in the chain homotopy so that n + 0 = n is definitional), but it still pervades the shuffle-level cross product.

2. simp_rw failing under ∑ binders. Several rewrites inside ∑ μ : Shuffle p q, ... require deeply nested conv_lhs => enter [2, x]; enter [2]; ... paths with erw instead of simp_rw, due to universe mismatches. Is there a cleaner way to handle rewrites under finset sums when the lemma is in a different universe?

3. ULift overhead from TopCat.toSSet. Singular simplices are ULift (Δ[n] ⟶ X) rather than Δ[n] ⟶ X, requiring .down/.up wrappers and ULift.ext in most simplex-level proofs. Is this expected and I should add a simp layer, or is there a way to avoid it?

4. Bridge lemmas between SimplexCategory and Fin. Combinatorial facts about shuffles are proved at the Fin level (succAbove, cast), but categorical goals involve (δ t ≫ eqToHom h).toOrderHom i. Translating between these requires ~20-line "bridge" lemmas per face map. Are there existing Mathlib lemmas that help here?

(EDIT: I still have a number of sorry'd combinatorial lemmas in Shuffle.lean.) The sign and injectivity lemmas for the insertion maps (insertLeftStep_injective, sign_insertLeftStep, the swapDiagonalSteps_* family, etc.) are all stated but not yet proved. These are purely combinatorial facts about monotone injections on Fin — (I have aristotle grinding these down right now).

This is my first Mathlib PR so any guidance on conventions, file structure, or where this should live would be very appreciated!
#homology > Homotopy invariance of singular homology

There are several sorries in this code, there are many erws and there are also several other places which the standard mathlib linters are going to flag as code smells, for example non-terminal simps. I know you mentioned some of these issues above but I guess I'm saying that the code isn't really ready for review. It's also the case that it's very hard to get LLM-written code into mathlib because the code quality is generally too poor right now and in many cases neither the human nor the AI is able to raise the standard to the level required.

Hey thanks for taking a look. I also have three of the other Eilenberg Steenrod axioms proven for singular homology (Relative Homology, Additivity and LES), I don't believe these are formalized previously. These are each self contained to a single file of a hundred lines or so each - would the path be to PR these first individually? Once these are merged I can return to assisting in the formalization of homotopy invariance to be ready for mathlib.
Almost all the ingredients for the formalization of homotopy invariance are already in pull requests...

Ok I see, yes proving homotopy invariance at the SSet level is much cleaner. Sorry, I had not seen your PRs in mathlib when I started working on this. Do you still think that formalizing the homology cross product / eilenberg zilber map will be useful or does it follow from your construction as well? Thanks!
It would certainly be useful to have the Eilenberg-Zilber theorem for simplicial modules.
(However, in order to get this into mathlib, using LLMs is not the best option.)

Is there be a better way to talk about dimension in chain complexes when you have dimensions that are not equal by definition but only by proposition? For example, I have alot of trouble dealing with statements such as C(Δ[p + 1] ⨯ Δ[q + 1]). d (p+ 1 + q+1) (p + q +1) = C(Δ[p + 1]). d x (id C(Δ[q+1]) + (-1) ^ (...) (id C(Δ[p + 1])) x (C(Δ[q+1].d) where I need to repeatedly use eqToHom (by omega) to show p +q + 1 = (p +1) + q in the codomain? Thanks!

You may use the same principle as in https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/4968c80f8ec7a3f0b233a0b530233199d061dc08/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/TotalComplex.lean#L148 (and other places). Roughly speaking, do not define something like X p ⊗ Y q ⟶ Z (p + q) but X p ⊗ Y q ⟶ Z n whenever p + q = n holds.
Thank you!

Hey, just an update, I've filled out all the combinatorial sorrys from before and refactored as you've mentioned, the cross product construction now is stated for abstract monoidal categories with forgetful functor instead of specialized to ModuleCat R.

Next I'll continue refactoring so that it depends on simplicial sets rather than on singular simplices for topology to match the simplicial homotopy PRs, and continue refactoring style to simplify arguments and get rid of erws and dsimps.

https://github.com/jeffrey-dot-li/lean-homology/blob/main/HomologyLean/SingularHomology/HomotopyInvariance.lean

Hey another quick update, I've packaged the Eilenberg Zilber map as

noncomputable def eilenbergZilberNatTrans :
    singChainTensor (C := C) ⟶ singChainProd (C := C) where
  app p := eilenbergZilber (C := C) p.1 p.2
  naturality _ _ f := (eilenbergZilber_natural f.1 f.2).symm

where singChainTensor and singChainTensor are functors SSet × SSet ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ

I do not know where to start. More importantly, I already have some code about non-degenerate simplices in Δ[p] ⊗ Δ[q] https://github.com/joelriou/topcat-model-category/blob/master/TopCatModelCategory/SSet/NonDegenerateProdSimplex.lean that I obviously plan to upstream to mathlib.

I would think that the better phrasing would be the following:

import Mathlib.AlgebraicTopology.AlternatingFaceMapComplex
import Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.Homotopy
import Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.TotalComplex

open AlgebraicTopology CategoryTheory.Limits

namespace CategoryTheory

variable {C : Type*} [Category* C]

variable (C) in
abbrev BisimplicialObject := SimplicialObject (SimplicialObject C)

namespace BisimplicialObject

@[simps!]
def diag : BisimplicialObject C ⥤ SimplicialObject C :=
  Functor.uncurry ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj (Functor.diag _)

variable [Preadditive C] [HasFiniteCoproducts C]

instance : (alternatingFaceMapComplex C).Additive := { }

open ComplexShape in
instance (K : ChainComplex (ChainComplex C ℕ) ℕ) :
    HomologicalComplex₂.HasTotal K (.down ℕ) := by
  intro n
  let f (pq : ((down ℕ).π (down ℕ) (down ℕ) ⁻¹' {n})) : Fin (n + 1) × Fin (n + 1) :=
    ⟨⟨pq.1.1, by
      have := pq.2
      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, π_def, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at this
      lia⟩, ⟨pq.1.2, by
      have := pq.2
      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, π_def, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at this
      lia⟩⟩
  have := Finite.of_injective f (fun _ _ ↦ by grind)
  infer_instance

noncomputable abbrev F₁ : BisimplicialObject C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ :=
  alternatingFaceMapComplex _  ⋙
    (alternatingFaceMapComplex C).mapHomologicalComplex _ ⋙
      HomologicalComplex₂.totalFunctor _ _ _ _

abbrev F₂ : BisimplicialObject C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ :=
  diag ⋙ alternatingFaceMapComplex C

-- `hom`, `inv`, `homotopyHomInvId`, and `homotopyInvHomId` must also be natural in `X`
def eilenbergZilber (X : BisimplicialObject C) :
    HomotopyEquiv (F₁.obj X) (F₂.obj X) := sorry

variable [Preadditive C]

end BisimplicialObject

end CategoryTheory

If anybody provides a clean proof of this sorry (and the naturality of all the data), this could be considered for addition to mathlib, as this implies some form of the Künneth formula for the homology of simplicial sets (and in particular for the singular homology of topological spaces).
Thanks will give this an attempt

Hey, wanted to give an update on my progress here. I now have the statement you gave 

noncomputable def eilenbergZilber (X : BisimplicialObject C) :
    HomotopyEquiv (F₁.obj X) (F₂.obj X) :=
  (bridge₁ X).symm.trans <| (eilenbergZilberNormalized X).trans <|
    homotopyEquivNormalizedMooreComplexAlternatingFaceMapComplex (A := C) (Y := diag.obj X)

compiling in lean without sorries, with F1 and F2 using your definitions on bisimplicial objects.

The proof uses the Dold - Kan correspondance to transport the homotopy equivilence to the normalized complex, then follows Eilenberg–Mac Lane, On the Groups H(Π,n)H(\Pi,n)H(Π,n), II: Methods of Computation Annals of Mathematics 60 (1954), 49–139. to define the homotopy equivilences
what naturality statement would you like to see regarding the homotopy equivilence? I will start working on that now to finish this proof

Code is here, all dependencies are in the EilenbergZilberTheorem folder https://github.com/jeffrey-dot-li/lean-homology/blob/3447f8d4d7275a9ec9af79462721a2f87899849c/HomologyLean/SingularHomology/EilenbergZilberTheorem/BisimplicialNormalized.lean#L777

Could you explain what proportion of the code was written by AI?
The definition https://github.com/jeffrey-dot-li/lean-homology/blob/3447f8d4d7275a9ec9af79462721a2f87899849c/HomologyLean/SingularHomology/EilenbergZilberTheorem/Bisimplicial.lean#L87 seems similar to https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/SimplexCategory/DeltaZeroIter.html#SimplexCategory.%CE%B4%E2%82%80Iter (a similar design which avoids eqToHom should probably be applied to ι_front also).
About the naturality statements, the meaning should be clear for the hom and inv fields of the homotopy equivalence, and the proof should be very easy. As everything is given by "universal" formulas, the same should apply to homotopyHomInvId and homotopyInvHomId. I do not think it is important at all to focus on this at this stage.
It would certainly be a lot of work to make the code land in the vicinity of mathlib standards. It is good to know that this was doable though, thanks for trying!
